blocks.text: The address “O Immanuel” in verse 8 recalls the sign in the preceding chapter. That earlier sign was presented to Ahaz as time-sensitive within a crisis, but the child’s immediate identity—and how that setting relates to Matthew’s later use of Immanuel—remain disputed. Isaiah 8 also moves among divine speech, the prophet’s first-person report, public warnings, and other voices; speaker and audience should therefore be identified from the immediate passage rather than assumed throughout the chapter.

Isaiah 8 is part of a book preserved in more than one ancient manuscript tradition. The Great Isaiah Scroll is an almost complete witness to all sixty-six chapters and broadly aligns with the Masoretic tradition, while also containing many spelling and substantive differences. Other Qumran Isaiah manuscripts and interpretive writings show that the book was actively transmitted and interpreted.
